title: The three cult-species are analogical, not univocal under one genus
source_text: VII. Praeterea observant Scholae Romanae Doctores has tres cultus species non esse univocas, id est, ejusdem rationis, nec sub eodem univoco genere contineri: sed esse tantum analogas propter quandam proportionis similitudinem, quae est inter excellentiam divinam & cultum qui illi debetur, & excellentiam creatam ac cultum qui illi respondet. Caeterum quemadmodum excellentia non dicitur univoce, & eadem ratione, de excellentia Dei & creaturarum: ita cultum debitum ob excellentiam docent non posse univoce dici de cultu Dei & creaturarum.
pass_a_gloss: Furthermore the Doctors of the Roman School observe that these three species of cult are not univocal, that is, of the same reason, nor contained under the same univocal genus: but are only analogical on account of a certain likeness of proportion, which is between divine excellence and the cult owed to it, and created excellence and the cult that answers to it. Moreover just as excellence is not said univocally, and by the same reason, of the excellence of God and of creatures: so they teach that the cult owed on account of excellence cannot be said univocally of the cult of God and of creatures.
pass_b_english: Roman doctors deny one univocal genus for the three cults—only analogy of proportion.
As ‘excellence’ is not univocal of God and creatures, neither is ‘cult’ owed for excellence.

choices.why: Analogical, not generic, unity of cult-kinds.
